alternate_names: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (foothill shrine)
festivals: Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Brahmotsavam (11 days, Phalguna / February-March)

history.dynasty: Vijayanagara (patronage; inscription of Krishnadevaraya); 11-storey gopuram by Raja Vasireddy Venkatadri Nayudu (1807-09)
history.period: Ancient (origin traced to the Pandava era per belief); current form 16th-19th century
history.summary: The Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, the Diguva Sannidhi (lower shrine) at the foot of the Auspicious Hill in Mangalagiri, is one of the eight mahakshetras of Narasimha and the 6th Nava Narasimha temple. Belief traces its origin to Yudhishthira, the eldest Pandava, who is said to have founded the chief stone image; the temple's history is also recorded in the Brahma Vaivarta Purana. It was patronized by the Vijayanagara rulers - an inscription of Krishnadevaraya, who visited the temple, survives at the site. Its signature is the 11-storey eastern gali gopuram, 153 feet high and 49 feet wide, built in 1807-09 by Raja Vasireddy Venkatadri Nayudu, devotee of Narasimha who ruled from Amaravati; legend says the leaning tower was straightened after architects dug a tank opposite it. The deity is worshipped with a 108-saligramam garland and a Dakshanavrutha Sankham (a conch believed to have been used by Krishna). The other two Narasimha forms at Mangalagiri are the Panakala Narasimha on the hill (the deity 'drinks' panakam/jaggery water) and Gandala Narasimha at the hilltop.

name: Diguva Mangalagiri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
town_description: Mangalagiri, meaning 'Auspicious Hill', is a town in Guntur district on the NH-16 corridor between Vijayawada (approx. 13 km) and Guntur (approx. 21 km). It is best known for its three Narasimha shrines - Panakala Narasimha on the hill, Lakshmi Narasimha at the foot, and Gandala Narasimha at the top - and for Mangalagiri handloom cotton sarees and fabrics.

travel.airport: Vijayawada International Airport (approx. 32 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Mangalagiri Railway Station (approx. 2.3 km); Vijayawada Junction (approx. 12-13 km) connects across India.
travel.road: On NH-16; APSRTC buses run from Vijayawada (approx. 13 km) and Guntur (approx. 21 km), with the Mangalagiri bus depot approx. 4 km from the temple. Local autos and taxis available.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when Andhra's weather is cooler; the 11-day Brahmotsavam in February-March is the most vibrant time. Verify before visiting, as timings can change on festival days.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 5:00 AM to 12:30 PM; evening 4:00 PM to 8:30 PM (verify). Footwear not allowed inside; no entry fee.
